DESCRIPTION: The Ascentis family of columns is the fourth generation of HPLC column technology from Supelco scientists. Ascentis columns are bonded on high purity, 100 Angstrom silica including 3, 5, and 10 micron particle size. Columns are designed for small molecule applications and are scalable from micro columns (1.0 mm I.D.) to preparative dimensions (50 mm I.D.). The family includes C18, C8, Phenyl, Si and embedded polar group phase, RP-Amide. Ascentis C18 is an extremely stable and reliable first choice HPLC column that gives symmetric peak shape and excellent retention even for difficult compounds. A dilute-and-shoot liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry method for urinary 18-hydroxycortisol quantification and its application in establishing reference intervals: This paper details the application of Ascentis® C18 columns in a clinical setting to measure cortisol levels in urine. The method provides a fast, accurate, and reliable way to assess patient hormonal profiles, critical for diagnosing endocrine disorders (Zhao et al., 2022). A Comparative Study on Analysis of Ginsenosides in American Ginseng Root Residue by HPLC-DAD-ESI-MS and UPLC-HRMS-MS/MS: Utilizing Ascentis® C18, this study compares different analytical methods for quantifying ginsenosides. It showcases the column?s adaptability and precision in natural product research, essential for ensuring the quality and efficacy of herbal medicines (Hsu et al., 2022). Validation of a Rapid and Easy-to-Apply Method to Simultaneously Quantify Co-Loaded Dexamethasone and Melatonin PLGA Microspheres by HPLC-UV: Highlighting the Ascentis® C18?s effectiveness in pharmaceutical formulations, this research demonstrates its capacity to analyze complex drug delivery systems, contributing to the development of more effective therapeutic solutions (Brugnera et al., 2022). Simultaneous determination of ivermectin, clorsulon and their related substances in an injectable finished product by a stability-indicating RP-HPLC method: This publication illustrates the application of the Ascentis® C18 in veterinary medicine, providing crucial insights into drug stability and composition which are vital for regulatory compliance and animal safety (Padivitage et al., 2022). •Excellent retention •Symmetric peak shape •High reproducibility •Complete LC-MS compatibility

DESCRIPTION: General description  This 22nd edition of the IUBMB-Nicholson Metabolic Pathways Chart features an enhanced ATP metabolism in mitochondria and chloroplasts.  It illustrates the sequences of reactions involved in different aspects of metabolism and how they are integrated. The backbone of the map is the Glycolytic Pathway, followed by the TCA (Krebs) Cycle and the ElectronTransport System, which together produce most of the energy (ATP) required for all life. Most other aspects of metabolism are associated with this backbone and are differentiated by the use of color. Human metabolism is distinguished by the use of black arrows. Some 550 reactions are identified by their IUBMB Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers which are then indexed.

DESCRIPTION:
Overview

AltraBio offers comprehensive omics data analysis services, leveraging expertise in bioinformatics, biostatistics, and biology. We provide in-depth analysis and interpretation of various omics data types, including genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics, to support your research and clinical objectives.


Key Benefits

  • Rigorous Quality Controls: Ensuring the integrity and reliability of your omics data.
  • Customized Statistical Analyses: Tailored to address the specific needs of your study.
  • Integrated Analysis: Combining multi-omics data with machine learning approaches for comprehensive insights.
  • Functional Analysis: Identification of biological processes and pathways relevant to your research questions.
  • In-Depth Biological Interpretation: Extracting meaningful insights and formulating new hypotheses.
  • Comprehensive Reporting: Clear and detailed reports summarizing findings and methodologies.
  • Interactive Results: Accessible via the WikiBioPath web interface for further exploration and visualization.

How It Works

Our omics data analysis process involves several key steps:

  1. Data Quality Assessment: Implementing methods to evaluate data quality and consistency with experimental design, addressing outliers and unrelated effects.
  2. Statistical Modeling: Identifying the most appropriate statistical models to address the biological questions of your study, considering factors such as donor, cell type, treatment, dose, and timepoints.
  3. Data Integration: Combining various data types (multi-omics, cytometry, medical data) using machine learning for biomarker identification, classification, and predictive modeling.
  4. Functional Analysis: Employing complementary methods to identify biological processes and pathways, reviewed for relevance to the study's context.
  5. Biological Interpretation: Evaluating results in light of the initial biological questions and integrating available scientific knowledge to understand underlying mechanisms.
  6. Reporting and Visualization: Providing comprehensive reports and interactive visualizations through the WikiBioPath interface, allowing clients to explore data further.

Applications

  • Research and Development: Support for basic and applied research in various biological fields.
  • Clinical Studies: Analysis of omics data from clinical trials to assess treatment efficacy and safety.
  • Diagnostic Development: Contribution to the development of diagnostic tools and assays based on omics data.

Why Choose AltraBio?

AltraBio's omics data analysis services offer a trusted and reliable solution for your analytical needs. Our commitment to excellence and innovation ensures that you receive high-quality results that drive your research and clinical projects forward.

DESCRIPTION: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), formerly known as non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), is the severe form of MASLD (metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease), which affects almost 25% of the world population with a high overlap of obesity and diabetes. The pathogenesis of MASH is complex in association with steatosis and hepatitis, followed by aggressive fibrosis, cirrhosis, and even cancer. This specialized panel contains a total of 29 targets, which are highly engaged in glucose (e.g., GLP1), lipid (e.g., THRβ), and bile acid (e.g., FXR) metabolisms, as well as inflammatory (e.g., VAP1), apoptotic (e.g., ASK1), and fibrotic (e.g., LOXL2) effects, all are critical therapeutic indicators for MASH drug discovery and development. This panel enables an understanding of the mechanism of action (MOA), which helps more efficacious drugs discovered against this difficult-to-treat liver disease.

The main advantage of using the IDMS technique is because isotope-labeled compounds have nearly the same physical properties as their non-labeled counterpart analog, and thus show identical behavior during the workup and sample preparation process. This helps in overcoming the problems of matrix effects generally encountered in the usual LC-MS/GC-MS analysis potentially resulting in biased results. By spiking the sample before workup with its isotope labeled analog, the loss of analyte that leads to matrix effects can be determined and compensated.  Legal Information<

DESCRIPTION: A Certified Snap-N-Spike® Solution appropriate for use as starting material in calibrators or controls for a variety of LC/MS or GC/MS applications from forensic analysis and clinical toxicology to urine drug testing and pharmaceutical research. Estazolam is a benzodiazepine prescribed for the short-term treatment of insomnia. Sold under trade names such as ProSom or Eurodin, estazolam is often abused recreationally to achieve a high or when long-term use is continued against physician advice. Estazolam in environmental trace analysis: A study employing ultra-performance liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) detailed the detection of Estazolam among other psychotropic medications in environmental samples, underscoring the method?s precision and application in monitoring environmental contamination by pharmaceutical residues (Wang et al., 2024). Estazolam and insomnia post-coronavirus disease: Research analyzed insomnia prevalence among COVID-19 survivors, identifying Estazolam as part of the therapeutic regimen. This study highlights the ongoing relevance of Estazolam in addressing sleep disorders associated with long-term recovery from significant health events (Lu et al., 2024). Comparative analysis of Estazolam for post-stroke insomnia: A network meta-analysis compared various treatments for post-stroke insomnia, including Estazolam, providing insights into its effectiveness relative to other therapeutic options. This study contributes to understanding optimal treatment strategies for insomnia in post-stroke patients (Song et al., 2023).

DESCRIPTION: MitoA is a ratiometric mass spectrometry probe that can be used for assessing changes in H2S within mitochondria in vivo. In a mouse model of acute myocardial infarction with MitoA administered prior to ischemia, the MitoN/MitoA ratio is increased only in the region of ischemia.

DESCRIPTION:
The Mass Spectrometry Resource (MSR) is a state-of-the-art biologic mass spectrometry facility providing access to all the necessary instrumentation for high-throughput, high accuracy protein identification, quantification and characterisation.
______________

Instrumentation:
In terms of equipment, MSR avails of several mass spectrometers in order to be able to cover almost all possible experimental workflows in mass spectrometry-based proteomics. These include:

- Thermo Fisher Q-Exactive 
- Thermo Fisher Orbitrap
- Thermo Fisher LTQ ion trap 
- Agilent 6520 Quadrupole-ToF
- Agilent 6460 Triple Quadrupole
- ABI 4800 Ultra MALDI/ToF-ToF with CovalX HM2 high-mass range detector
- Bruker HCTUltra II ETD ion trap.

The AB Sciex 4800 MALDI-Tof/Tof mass spectrometer with a CovalX HM2 high mass-range detector is applied to gel-based and off-line liquid chromatography (LC)-based, high throughput MALDI-MS/MS proteomic workflows or, in linear mode, to accurate determination of the mass of intact proteins or protein complexes up to 1.2 Megadaltons.

The Q-Exactive,  LTQ-Orbitrap, the ion traps, the quadrupole time-of-flight and a triple quadrupole mass spectrometers cover all possible needs in liquid-chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. 

Furthermore, the MSR offers access to LC-based workflows supporting the multi-dimensional protein identification technology (MudPIT) and a nano-LC system coupled to a MALDI target loading robot to support off-line LC MALDI-MS.

Software suite
Raw data files generated by each mass spectrometer are subjected to database search with the appropriate algorithm (Mascot, TurboSequest, Spectrum Mill) and database.

DESCRIPTION: Phenytoin-d10 is intended for use as an internal standard for the quantification of phenytoin by GC- or LC-MS. Phenytoin is an anticonvulsant agent and active metabolite of fosphenytoin. Phenytoin is formed from fosphenytoin by tissue phosphatases. It inhibits neuronal voltage-gated sodium channels in a voltage-dependent manner. Phenytoin reduces the neuronal firing frequency and decreases the amplitude of excitatory post-synaptic potentials (EPSPs) in electrically stimulated rat corticostriatal slices. It protects against seizures induced by maximal electroshock (MES) in mice. Formulations containing phenytoin have been used in the treatment of tonic-clonic seizures and status epilepticus.
